elements.str: Origin of the fabulous things of the ancients.
Inmost things are signified by the face.
Two faces were as it were induced on me... When the Angels perceive that their faces are received, they know that the man is dead.
With the ancients, the face = internal things, because internal things shine forth through the face. In ancient times their faces agreed exactly with their internals...
When charity shone from the face, they said that the face was elevated; but when the contrary, they said that the face fell.
Their faces appeared sharp, beautiful enough.
They spoke... by innumerable changes of the expression and face...
The intellectual things of Spirits and Angels flow into the left part or the face, and the voluntary things into the right.
The deceitful appear to have a broad face, four or five times as broad as the faces of others.
Their faces are worse than that of a dead man.
They sometimes appear to themselves to have a shining face.
Their faces are like a round cake, broad.
Spirits who belong to a certain internal province of the face.
The charity which shines from the face is not of the face...
Spirits who... expressed their meaning by changes induced on my face...
) = the Lord's mercy towards universal mankind.
They looked to the faces of Sodom
= all the interiors of man, both evil and good; because these shine forth from the face. Here, therefore,
being predicated of Sodom, = evil interiors which are of the love of self.
When Angels are presented to view, their interiors shine forth from the face.
Men who in the life of the body have been merely natural, when presented to view in the other life according to that state, appear hairy over nearly the whole face.
For it is the animus which appears in the face. Explained.
The face with the Angels and with the most ancients. Described.
) = when these things ceased; thus when the state was changed.
The Societies which constitute the province of the face...
They were allowed to effigy a face in various ways by influx.
From the affections of the animus, which present themselves to view in the face...
In human faces, in which for the most part the affections effigy themselves, no two are exactly alike.
That the face is the image of the animus...
= the interiors, thus the thoughts and affections.
At this day there is scarcely any general involuntary sense left in the face.
see his faces as the faces of God
all good, which, when it flows in, gives affection with perception.
= the interiors, thus the affections of good and truth which shine forth from the face.
The Spirits who are at the face are of diverse genius, according to correspondence with the sensories there...
On the correspondence of the face with the Grand Man.
The Lord lift up His faces
= that from the Divine affection of love He has mercy.
The faces of the men of another world described.
Whatever a man wants to hide, contracts his face...
) = that truth is not seen at all.

The Angels do not see the faces of men in their material, but in their spiritual form; that is, in the form presented by the affections and consequent thoughts; these also are what cause the real face with man...
The Natural is as a face...

Without such an interior face, or such a plane, a man in the body cannot think at all about the things which are above sensuous things; for he sees them there as when a man sees the affections and thoughts in another's face, not attending to the face itself.
The faces of Spirits and Angels are formed from and according to the exterior Natural. Described.
They lie there face down wards.
The quality of Spirits and Angels... in the Rational, appears from the face and its beauty.
He had no face, but something blackly bearded instead of a face.
These for a face had a direful grate of teeth.
To be devoid of a face = that there is nothing of rational life; for when no face appears, it is a sign that there is no correspondence of the interiors with the Grand Man.
The face represents the interiors of man, thus his spiritual and celestial things, that is, the things which are of faith and charity.
Ye shall not see my faces
= the Divine love, is evident from the Lord's face when He was transfigured, (which)
) = to enjoy peace and good from mercy.
He lifted up portions from his faces for them
) = goods applied to everyone from mercy.
After I have seen thy faces
I did not think to see thy faces
) = that he had not been in hope concerning the influx of his love.
Joseph fell upon the faces of his father
fall upon the faces of anyone
The face (of the woman of Mercury) was beautiful, but smaller than the faces of the women of our Earth.
Good forms the faces of the Angels.
The Spirits of Mars are represented with the face in Heaven, and the body in the World of Spirits...
With them the face acts as one with the thought, so that the affection itself of the thought shines forth from the face.
(The faces of the inhabitants of Mars are like the faces of the inhabitants of our Earth, but the lower part of the face is black, not from a beard...)
= no mercy, no peace, and no good. Explained.
The face of man's spirit is entirely according to that which reigns universally with him.
= the interiors as to the affections and the consequent thoughts (References); and as
= the affections, they also = the desires.
He drove them out from the faces of Pharaoh
= the interiors as to the affections, thus the will.
= the interiors, especially as to the affections; thus
The Angels of Jupiter came to me... They had an influx into the face, so that the face concurred with every particular...
The faces of the inhabitants of Jupiter are like the faces of the men of oar Earth, white, but more beautiful; sincerity and modesty shine out from them.

When the Spirits of Jupiter were with me, the faces of the inhabitants of our Earth used to appear less; because the idea flowed in which those Spirits had about their own faces, that they were larger; for when they live as men they believe that after death their faces will be larger, and round in form; and therefore... when they become Spirits, they seem to themselves to have a larger face. The reason they believe that their faces will be larger, is that they say the face is not the body, because they speak and present their thoughts through it; and because the mind is thus as it were seen through it; hence they have an idea of the face as being the mind in form; and as they know that they will be wiser after their life in the world, they believe that the form of the mind, that is, the face, will be larger.
They also believe that after death they will perceive a fire which will warm their faces. Explained.
On this account they frequently wash and cleanse their faces; and also carefully preserve them from the heat of the sun...

They said that the faces of the men of our Earth are not beautiful; and wondered that the faces of some are full of warts and pimples, and are in other respects disfigured; and said that none such appear among them.

In their Earth the faces of almost all are smiling and cheerful; because they have no solicitude about future things, and have no care for worldly things... The reason their faces are prominent about the lips, is that the most of their speech is effected by the face... and also because they never dissemble... therefore they do not force their faces.
The face was formed wholly to effigy the things which man thinks and wills; hence the face is called the effigy and index of the animus.
(The inhabitants of Jupiter) are very willing that their faces should be seen, because hence their mind appears...
His face as the aspect of lightning
Thou shalt not have other gods before My faces
when predicated of God, = love, mercy, peace, good; thus the Lord Himself...
in the Word, = the interiors, especially the affections. References.
in the Word, = good itself. References.
(The Spirits of the moon) appeared of a face not unhandsome, but longer than the faces of all other Spirits.
when predicated of Jehovah, = the Divine good of the Divine love, or mercy. And as the Divine good of the Divine love is Jehovah Himself or the Lord, to be
seen at the faces of the Lord Jehovah
) has a like signification to being seen by the Lord.

because by the face are signified the interiors which are of the life, thus which are of the thought and affection, and especially which are of the faith and love. The reason is that the face is formed to the image of the interiors of man, to the end that those things which are of the internal man may appear in the external, thus that the things which are of the Spiritual world may appear before the sight in the natural world... And therefore, in the Original Language,

is a general term which is applied to describe the affections... Hence it is, that in that language, with adjunctives, it means nigh to, with, before, on account of, and also what is contrary; thus whatever is in himself, from himself, for himself, and against himself; for the face is the man himself, or that which is in him and appears.
= the Divine good of the Divine love, and the Divine truth from this Divine good; for these are in Him, and are Himself. Illustrated.
Hence it is that the Lord as to the Divine Human is called
the Angel of the faces of Jehovah
Their faces, of a man to his brother
= the interiors; here, mental view and conjunction.
the mercy-seat shall be the faces of the cherubs

They who are elevated by the Lord (and the Angels) continually turn their faces to the Lord, because the Lord keeps them conjoined with Himself through the good of love; but they who are not elevated turn their faces from the Lord.
when predicated of the Lord, = everything which is from the Divine love; as innocence, peace, joy; thus Heaven itself with man and Angel.
) = thus the Lord's presence with peace and with heavenly joy from mercy.
when predicated of man and Angel, = the interiors which are of the will and of the understanding thence, thus which are of love and of faith thence. References.
, Explained. (as to the various parts of the face).
= the Lord as to Divine good; for
) = the Divine truth from the Divine good.
in the internal sense, = to love.
One thing is signified by to
) = upon the external separated from what is internal in which was Moses and the nation he was over...
Thou canst not see My faces
For the Lord is the face itself of Jehovah. Explained.
) = Divine internal things upon external ones.
The sparkling of the skin of Moses' face
From their faces (in the Sixth Earth) they see whether they agree in minds
All who form one angelic Society have a face that is like in general, but is not like in particular. Explained.

In Heaven all the interior affections appear and shine forth from the face; for the face there is their external and representative form; to have another face than that of one's own affections does not exist in Heaven.

A face as of an Angel appeared to me, which was varied according to the affections of good and truth, such as exist with those who are in one Society. The variations lasted a long time; and I observed that the same face in general remained as a plane, and that the rest were only derivations and propagations thereof...
The interiors make the face of an Angel and a Spirit; and in the Spiritual World... it is the face which determines (the quarters).
If anyone dissents, he must turn away his face.

As heavenly loves open the interiors to the Lord, all the Angels turn their faces to the Lord; for in the Spiritual World it is the love which turns the interiors of everyone to itself, and wherever it turns the interiors it also turns the face; for the face there acts as one with the interiors, it being their external form.
Especially when they look at each other face to face...

When the spirit first enters the World of Spirits... he has a like face... But afterwards the face is changed, and becomes... like his ruling love... For the face of the spirit differs very much from the face of the body; the face of the body is from the parents; but the face of the spirit from the affection... I have seen some who were recently from the world, and knew them from their face and speech; but when they were seen afterwards, I did not know them. They who had been in good affections were seen with a beautiful face; but they who had been in evil affections, with a deformed face; for, regarded in itself, the spirit of man is nothing but its own affection, the external form of which is the face. The reason the faces are changed, is that in the other life it is not allowable for anyone to counterfeit affections which are not properly his own, thus neither to induce on himself faces contrary to the love in which he is... Hence it is that the faces of all are the forms and effigies of their affections...
The faces of hypocrites are changed later than the faces of the rest...
Therefore the more interior the affection is... the more beautiful is the face.

So far as anyone acts and speaks according to another's love, the latter appears... with a full, cheerful, living face; but so far as anyone acts and speaks contrary to his love, his face begins to be changed, to be obscured, and not to appear.
Hence the face of one can never be exactly like that of another; for the face is the image of the animus; and in the Spiritual World it is the image of the reigning love.

They who have not acted clandestinely, but have wanted all things they thought to appear openly... in Heaven have faces which shine; and in the face, from that light, each of their affections and thoughts appears as in form... While they are speaking, the face is a little obscured, but when they have done speaking, the same things which they spoke appeal simultaneously in the face in full view.
Communication with others there takes place according to the conversion of the face...
His face which flashed as the sun
Like a man whose face and hands are bare.
The Lord sees and looks at everyone face to face...
The interiors of the face are the brains.
These two worlds are entirely similar in external appearance... But as to their internal complexion they are entirely dissimilar.
He then turns his face from the devil to the Lord; and when he turns his face to the Lord, love and wisdom are given him. These enter man by the face...
Such appear there like faces without a head...
Not allowed to see the Divine Providence on the face.
His face as the sun shining in his power
) = the Divine love and the Divine wisdom, which are Himself...
or of the Lord = the Divine itself in its essence, which is the Divine love and the Divine wisdom, thus Himself.
They who constitute the face, with all its organs of sense (are meant by the tribes of Israel in
Their faces were as the faces of men
= wisdom and intelligence. ( = the affections of truth.
in the Word, = that which is with man interiorly, because the face is the type of his animus formed to correspondence; hence
The Angels were impelled to fall on their faces.
see the face of... the Lord

does not mean to see His face; because no one can see His face, as He is in His Divine love and Wisdom, and live... for to see His face, as He is in Himself, would be as if one should enter into the sun... But the Lord sometimes presents Himself to be seen out of His Sun. Explained... But by their seeing His face is not here meant to see His face in this manner, but to see the truths which are in the Word from Him; and through them to Know and acknowledge Him. Explained.
They seemed... as if their faces were unconnected with their bodies.
(Origin of the harder face of the male.)

That no two men have exactly the same love, may appear from the infinite variety of human faces; faces being types of loves; for that faces are changed and varied according to the affections of love is known...
(The faces of a husband and a wife from the Third Heaven. Described.)
Can the love of the sex stop at the face of a woman?
I observed as it were the unity of their souls in their faces.
They had faces as of steel...
He no longer endures to look his consort directly in the face.
They had round faces, which glistened like the scales of a shell.
(The doorkeeper said), I was told that I should know (whom to admit) by their faces... All the Angels can see from the faces of others the delights of their hearts...
At a distance they seem to have white faces consisting only of skin...
They appeared to me... to have faces of chalk.
There are two faces to this faith...
As a face before the work...
In Jupiter etc. they speak by the face.
(The faces of men in Jupiter. Described.)
That such bristly, misty, fiery, and also such beautiful faces... originate from the inspection of the Angels.
The general natural influx projects itself especially into the face, and into the region of the loins. The other parts depend more upon the will... but not ho the face...

The general natural sense first occupied the whole face, afterwards the left side of the face, and at last only the ear... The changes of the affections, or of celestial things, are of the right side of the face, (and) those of spiritual things, are of the left side of the face... It is not allowable to proceed from... spiritual to celestial things, and therefore the right side of the face is guarded by the Lord, to prevent the influx from the left side extending itself thither...
How, at this day, the case is with influx into faces, which influxes are not natural... See
On the face of an ape.
Spirits who think about future things... appear with a broad face; but it is not a face, but only the broad area of a face...
Hypocrites have no face. Described. See
That the faces of men are altered there.
Then, good conjoined with truth forms the face.
That all are Known who are alike, whatever face they may have... The reason is that the whole thought of one is communicated to another, and the affection of the thought makes the face.
He could induce on himself various different faces...
(Good Spirits are instructed by changes in their faces, if they have not thought well.)
(They who are in good but not in truths) appear to have faces covered with monstrous prominences Hence it was evident, that the Intellectual conjoined with the Voluntary appears in the face.
They who appear in the world with faces good and gentle... but inwardly think evil about all...
The Divine love from which the Lord flows in, is meant by
); the Divine truth with which the Lord flows in, is meant by
Jehovah make His faces to shine upon thee
; and the Divine good with which He flows in, is meant by
Jehovah lift up His faces upon thee.
when predicated of the Lord, = the Divine love from which is the Divine good in Heaven. Illustrated.
in the proper sense, is the Sun of the angelic Heaven...
= the interior things of the Church, of the Word, and of worship. Illustrated.
when predicated of man, = the animus and his affection, thus the interiors which belong to his mind. Explained, Illustrated.
References to passages on the subject of the face.
= humiliation of heart, because it corresponds to this humiliation.
= the things which are revealed in the Word.
= the Divine love, and enlightenment thence.
= to the life, and to the acknowledgement.
cover the face that he see not the earth
As the Angels turn their faces to their consorts, they are, in the same proportion, in a state of wisdom...
The faces of the Angels are types of their minds
The face of a Spirit is changed according to the changes of his affections.
Man has two faculties, the will and the understanding...
A Spirit receives much more excellent faculties... The same faculties remain, but are much more perfect...
The vessels of little children... are mere capacities of receiving.
According to the capacity of each person.
The body impeded the interior exercise of his faculties.
The rational man is not born with man, but only the capacity of becoming rational.
Gives the capacity of knowing, thinking, and understanding.
In consequence of hereditary evil, all man's faculties are in a contrary direction...

Souls who desire to see the glory of the Lord, as to their exterior senses and faculties are lulled into a kind of sweet sleep; and then their interior senses and faculties are roused into an eminent degree of wakefulness...
Begins to... have the faculty of reflecting...
Little children, when they come into the other life... have only the capacity of knowing...
Perception is nothing else than the Divine influx into the intellectual faculty.
According to his state and capacity.
Everyone according to his Own capacity
Among the eminent faculties which man has in himself, although he is not aware of it, is...
As man after death comes into these faculties...
By the faculty which they possessed as men...
in the Hebrew, means the faculties from which these truths and goods are derived.
All the life of man consists in the faculty that he can think and that he can will...
Still they are in the capacity of being intelligent and wise.
These can be in no enlightenment, although they have an imaginative and perceptive faculty. This faculty is twofold...
They can reason about these things, because they are in some capacity of knowing them, but in no affection of doing them.
Whenever the opportunity is given, it becomes an external act.
The more exterior a man's faculties are, the more general they are...
He would thus be deprived of his means.
By which he is in the capacity of thinking and speaking...
The ability of the Celestial of the Spiritual. Signified.
Every man whatever... is endowed with the capacity of understanding whether they are truths.
He who is in good is in the faculty of clearly seeing the truths which... Explained.

Truth in powers means in the capacities of receiving, thus according to the capacities; but the capacities or powers of receiving truth are entirely according to good... For when the Lord flows in with good, He also flows in with the capacity. Explained.
Every man who is of a sane mind, is in the capacity of receiving truths; but they who turn themselves to evil extinguish this capacity; whereas they who turn themselves to good elevate this capacity.

Every man possesses the capacity of perceiving whether a thing is so, or is not so; the capacity of concluding inwardly in himself... causes a thing to be perceived. This capacity can in no case exist unless there is an influx from the Spiritual World; and the gift of one man in this respect is superior to that of another...
The Internal from the Natural acquired the capacities of receiving good, because they are from itself. Signified.
As they have not closed the interiors, they are in the capacity of receiving goods and truths.
Thus the capacity of thinking and willing remains, but against truth and good.
They who can think above sensuous things

elements.injection1: if the things in their memories are in orderly arrangement

elements.str: The capacity of understanding and perceiving is according to the extension thither; that is, according to the influx thence.
They would seize the possessions of all.
It is said in the capacity of receiving the truth of good and the good of truth, because no others are in this capacity except those who have lived the life of charity; this life gives that capacity.
Reception and appropriation according to the capacity of each one. Signified.
It does not mean the acquiring... of possessions for the future.
It is the light which gives the capacity of understanding.
He who does not renounce all things that belong to him
) = him who does not love the Lord above all things.
But still they are in the capacity of perceiving and understanding; and also in the capacity of receiving in proportion as they desist from evils.
Everyman... is in the capacity of understanding truth Divine, and thence in the capacity of receiving it, in proportion as he desists from evils...
Hence good has faculty, but not determinate except by truth. Determinate faculty is actual power.

With the evil, the Lord... is present in general, by which presence they have the capacity of thinking and willing; and also of receiving faith and charity; but only in the proportion that they desist from evils.

By intelligence and wisdom is not meant the faculty of thinking and reasoning... but there is meant the faculty of seeing and perceiving truths and goods... This faculty does not exist except with those who are in enlightenment from the Lord.
In man there is only the capability that it may be done.
That all, of whatever capability they may be, ought to ascribe all things to the Lord. Signified.
All have the capacity of understanding and being wise... All have not indeed an equal capacity of being wise, but they equally have it.
) = all the truths and goods of the Church.
The things that belong to him,
in the internal sense, are spiritual riches and wealth, which are Knowledges from the Word... Here, by
the things that belong to him
are meant all things which are of his Own intelligence; and therefore to
renounce all things that belong to him
is to attribute nothing of intelligence and wisdom to himself.
... = the things which are of intelligence and wisdom...
They are deprived of the capacity of thinking what is true...
They have thereby become capacities of receiving Heaven...
Some suppose that the rich cannot be received unless they renounce their possessions and become like the poor.
According to their capacity of reception.
These two faculties, freedom and reason...

The very faculty of thinking rationally... is not man's... Upon this faculty depends human reason... Man by this faculty either is in the light of Heaven... It is otherwise if the man by this faculty should have perverted the lower parts of his understanding; such a man indeed possesses this faculty...

(Therefore) man has two faculties of life, from one of which he has an understanding, and from the other a will. The faculty from which he has understanding... and the faculty from which he has will... The fact that a man is not justly wise, and does not love rightly, does not take away the faculties, but only closes them... If, therefore, these faculties were taken away, it would involve the destruction of everything human... Hence it appears that the Divine resides with man in these two faculties, which are the faculty of being wise, and the faculty of loving; that is, in the ability.
The reciprocity considered in its faculty...

The faculty of thinking and willing alone remaining; the faculty of thinking, from rationality, and the faculty of willing, from freedom; which two faculties every man has from the Lord, nor are they ever taken away. These two faculties are possessed equally by devils and by Angels...
The distinction between the interior faculties of the mind... Or the distinction between the exterior faculties, which belong to the body...

There are two faculties from the Lord with man, by which he is distinguished from beasts. One faculty is, that he is able to understand what truth is and what good is; this is called rationality, and it is the faculty of his understanding. The other faculty is, that he is able to do what is true and good; this faculty is called freedom, and it is the faculty of his will... By virtue of these two faculties a man is a man... Man has these two faculties from the Lord, and has them continually from Him; nor are they taken away; for were they taken from him his humanity would perish. In these two faculties the Lord is with every man, both with the good and with the evil; they are the Lord's dwelling in the human race; hence it is that every man... lives to eternity. But the Lord's dwelling with man is nearer in proportion as the man by means of these faculties opens the higher degrees...

The faculty of receiving spiritual light... From this faculty of rationality it is that man... is able not only to think, but also to speak from thought; and afterwards from his other faculty, which is called freedom... he is able to do those things which he thinks...
The natural degrees, without the higher degrees, possess no faculty of thinking...

This power (the sensuous man) gets from a faculty proper to every man, the faculty of being able to understand truth if he chooses; this faculty makes all the distinction. Still, many, by the abuse of this faculty, have rendered themselves lower than the beasts.
Every man is born into the faculty of understanding truths to the inmost degree.
Rationality, which is the faculty that is capable of elevation...

That the origin of evil is from the abuse of the faculties which are proper to man, and are called rationality and freedom. By rationality is meant the faculty of understanding truths and thereby falsities... and by freedom is meant the facility of thinking, willing, and doing these things freely... Every man... has these two faculties, and they are from the Lord; and they are not taken away from him; and from them comes the appearance that man thinks, speaks, wills, and acts as from himself; and the Lord dwells in these faculties with every man... and through these faculties... man is able to be reformed and regenerated...
That an evil man enjoys these two faculties equally with a good man.
In the faculty or in the power of being able to will.
That an evil man abuses these faculties to confirm evils and falsities; and that a good man uses them to confirm goods and truths.
The affection of truth and the perception of truth are two faculties of the understanding...
That the faculty of understanding, which is called rationality; and the faculty of acting, which is called freedom, still remain.

Man has the faculty of acting, which is called freedom, and the faculty of understanding, which is called rationality. It is from the abuse of these faculties that man can seem in externals different from what he is in internals...
Man is born... with the capacity of becoming spiritual...
That by means of these two faculties a man can be reformed and regenerated, so far as he can be led to acknowledge that all good and truth... are from the Lord.
(Thus) these two faculties... are from the Lord, and not from man.
That the conjunction of the Lord with man... is effected by means of these two faculties.

That the Lord guards these two faculties in man unimpaired and as sacred... (For) without these two faculties man would not have understanding and will... And without these two faculties man could not be conjoined with the Lord... And, further, without these two faculties man would not have immortality... Explained seriatim.
These faculties are as it were implanted in man; for his humanity itself is in them.
Still, they have not lost the faculties themselves. From experience.

It is only from the Lord that man has ability to think, speak, and reason; for he has this ability from the two faculties called freedom and rationality; and man has these faculties from the Lord alone.
Man possesses the faculty of understanding arcana of wisdom like the Angels themselves.
Therefore (profaners) have no longer rationality in faculty or in power...
Man would then... lose his two faculties called freedom and rationality...
In every man, good or evil, there are two faculties, one of which makes the understanding, and the other the will... (The former) faculty is called rationality...

Since these two faculties are perpetual, and are continuous from primes to ultimates in everything man thinks and does; and as they are not in man from himself... Remove these faculties from any particular... and you will not be able to think or speak it as a man.
As these faculties are in man from the Lord, and are not appropriated to man as his; for what is Divine cannot be appropriated to man as his...
As they are in the faculty of thinking and acting, they cannot die.
The image and likeness of God... remain implanted in his two faculties, called freedom and rationality.
From which faculty earth is earth.
Spiritual life is (then) extinguished in the will, but it remains in the understanding, or rather in the faculty of understanding. By the latter, man is distinguished from beasts.
That they cannot take away from those who are not in the faith of charity the faculty of understanding and willing truth and good... Signified.
(They said), Man is born... faculty and inclination; faculty to know, and inclination to love...
That from creation there has been implanted in both sexes a faculty and inclination to be able and to want to be conjoined as into one.
Whence they have an inclination and faculty...
With the sole difference (between him and a beast) that he has the faculty of elevating his understanding... and also the faculty of elevating his will...
What is the cause of faculty with the Angels enduring to eternity...
When faculty ceases with the husband...
To acquire the property necessary to support a house and family.
God, with the faculty of generating, is in man perpetually.
Still, God resides in their highest parts... and gives them the faculty of willing good and of understanding truth; a faculty that every man has... That the evil also have this faculty...
His universal or external presence causes man... to enjoy the faculty of knowing, understanding, and speaking... He also enjoys the faculty of willing and doing...
There are four faculties; the soul, the rational mind, the natural mind, and sensation.
(I replied) that it is not their life, but it is the faculty of being able to reason and understand...
That there are distinct faculties, or lives, one within the other.
Inauguration into the first plane, or first faculty...
The worst infernal Spirits have the faculty of understanding truth.
= the Knowledges of good and truth, by which comes intelligence.

When the spiritual mind is closed, the light of Heaven can flow into the natural mind only through chinks, whence it has the faculty of thinking, reasoning, and speaking; and also the faculty of understanding truths; but not the faculty of loving them. Explained. See
The faculty of understanding truth, and perceiving good, is never destroyed with man. From experience.

The faculty of receiving good and truth is continually given to man; and also flows in, in proportion as man, from the faculty which is also given him, removes the evils which stand in the way; and the faculty itself appears as if it were of the man, although it is of the Lord.

That the capacity of understanding the truths of the Word was destroyed... Signified. Every man indeed has the capacity of understanding truths; for it is this capacity by which man is distinguished from beasts. This, too, is left with every man...
The two faculties, which are called knowledge and affection...
In order that (all) these faculties may come forth in effect and in use, they have been made and wonderfully organized...
3. They could take away all the faculty of thinking...
There is nothing in man except the faculty of receiving...
is the faculty of being able to understand truth, and of being able to will good.

the waters shall fail from the sea, the river shall be dried up,
The waters were in going and failing
= the apparent failure and privation of truth.
= the failure of Knowledges. References... How truth... afterwards fails so as to scarcely appear...
There is a failing of the spirits...
His heart failed, because he did not believe them
= a failing of the life; and because it is said of Jacob... it = a failing of the natural life; and
= that truths failed... That they entirely failed, is signified by its being said that
they went three days in the wilderness.
Wherefore, when these things fail, the spiritual life labours and suffers...
How the case is with the temptation which comes forth through the failing of truth... If good fails, it is as if food fails; and if truth fails, it is as if drink fails.
This chapter treats of a third temptation, which is caused by good failing; the lack of bread and flesh = the lack of good.
= the lack of the Knowledges of truth and of good.
That they would expire in consequence of the failure of delight and of good. Signified...
= the lack of good; here, of the pleasures of good.
In this chapter it treats of a fourth temptation, caused by truth failing.
There was no water for the people to drink
= the lack of truth, and thence of refreshment.
This longing is kindled according to the lack of truth...

The failure of spiritual good and truth was signified by rain not being given for three years and a half during the reign of Ahab, insomuch that the bread and water failed... Hence it was that the devastation of good and truth was represented by the failure of bread and water.
Lest perchance the land be desolate
= a failing then, and but little spiritual life...
= a failing and but little spiritual life; for when

is said of the Church in man, it = the failing of truth and good, thus also the failing of spiritual life. As to there being a failing and but little spiritual life if falsities and evils were to be hastily removed, the case is this...
The failure of truth, and the consequent vastation of the Church. Signified.
The fallacies which prevail with many on account of the want of knowledges...
For My name's sake hast laboured, and hast not fainted
) = the study and exertion to procure and also to teach the things of religion and its doctrine.
They shall not hunger any more or thirst any more
= that hereafter goods and truths shall not be wanting to them.
= not to have a lack of good; and

The wives said, Ability does not fail while the man loves the wife from intelligence; but it does fail if he does so from insanity; intelligence consists in loving the wife alone, and with this love ability does not fail; whereas insanity consists in not loving the wife, but the sex, and with this love ability fails.
= as far as they were able.
She that hath many children hath failed
= the failure of the Knowledges of good and truth.
There is no want to them that fear Him
) = those who love to do the Lord's commandments.

Their plenary deficiency is signified by
they have failed in the streets of the city

) = no truths in the natural man.
The lack of truth even to despair, and still the longing for it, is signified by,
Hungry and thirsty, their soul fainted in them
That the man who is in falsities of evil will endeavour to deprive him who is in truth from good, is signified by,
the fool speaketh foolishness, to make empty the soul, and to cause it to fail

In that day shall the beautiful maidens and the young men faint for thirst
Growing attenuate and faint by its incomprehensibility...
In the other life it fades into what is excrementitious.
Cannot fail to be dissolved into such things...
According to what is fair. Signified.
Acts in equality or unity with these two.
On those who are in natural good, but not in the perception of what is good and fair.
The fourth state is when he is affected with love, and illuminated with faith.
The sixth state is when from faith and thence from love, he speaks truths and does goods.
The very essence and life of faith is the Lord alone...

The progress of faith with those who are being created anew... They receive life from the Lord through faith; first through the faith of the memory, which is scientific faith; next through faith in the understanding, which is intellectual faith; and afterwards through faith in the heart, which is the faith of love, or saving faith. (These kinds of faith here represented.)
Love and faith in the internal man are circumstanced as are heat and light in the external corporeal man...
The Lord's mercy affects... the understanding with truth or faith.
... and it is said of faith that it shall
Scarcely any love, and therefore scarcely any faith. Signified.
The celestial Angels do not know what faith is, except that which is of love.
Love and faith can never be separated...

Thus they who are in love are also in faith... But the life of faith without love is circumstanced as is the light of the sun without heat... But faith from love is circumstanced as is the light of the sun in the time of spring... No faith, and faith without love, are also compared by the Lord to
Those who say they have faith, but live otherwise...

They who have separated faith from love, do not even know what faith is. When they are in the idea of faith, some know no otherwise than that it is mere thought; some that it is thought directed to the Lord; a few, that it is the doctrine of faith. But faith is not only the Knowledge of all things embraced in the doctrine of faith, and the acknowledgement of these things, but it is especially obedience to all things which it teaches... If a man is not in the love of the Lord and in the love of the neighbour, he is not in faith.
Now, when man is vivified by love and faith...
The things which are from the Lord have life in themselves, because they have faith in Him.
Scientifics animated by faith from the Lord. Signified.
is predicated of the things of faith.
It is the fifth state in which man speaks from faith, which is of the understanding...
Faith which is of the understanding is called
As the most ancients called the conjunction of... faith and love a marriage...
As faith is being conjoined with love...
So that he may have an undoubting faith.
Now the things of faith make one with those of love. Signified.
Adam in paradise = the faith in the Lord of the Most Ancient Church. Signified.
A spiritual man acknowledges truth and good... from faith; and from this he also acts... A celestial man... acknowledges no faith but that which is from love; and from this he also acts.
To scrutinize the things of faith in the Lord, whether they were so. Treated of.
Thus faith, that is, all wisdom and intelligence, would perish.
But with this man... that is, his descendants, the midst of the garden was faith.
(The members of the Most Ancient Church) were not allowed to think from sensuous and scientific things about anything that was of faith...

The more interiorly celestial of the celestial Angels do not admit of the mention of faith... and if it is mentioned by others, instead of faith they perceive love, with a difference known only to themselves; thus whatever is of faith they derive from love and charity; still less can they endure to hear anything rational, and least of all anything scientific about faith... and therefore when anything is said about faith, they merely reply that it is so, or that it is not so, because they perceive from the Lord. Signified.
For to reason about faith is to doubt and deny.
The Lord alone gives faith, and thus is faith.
To provide against his having power to enter into any arcanum of faith. Signified.

Faith or truth is of the understanding; from love or good they perceived what is of faith or what is of truth... But with the postdiluvians, and with those who live now, there is no love... but still there can exist faith, or the understanding of truth; and from faith or the understanding of truth they can be brought to a kind of charity...
The Most Ancient Church through love had faith in the Lord...
As it was faith through which charity was afterwards to be implanted...

The Most Ancient Church acknowledged no other faith than that which was of love to the Lord and towards the neighbour; through this love from the Lord they had faith, or the perception of all things which belonged to faith; and therefore they were unwilling to mention faith, lest it should be separated from love. Signified.
What is it that is done by faith, or knowledge, Knowledge, and the doctrine of faith, but that man does as it teaches The primary thing it teaches is charity.
Faith, too, is celestial when it is from love.
When men are thinking about a single article of faith, they make it the principal thing. (Hence heresy.)

They made no distinction between love which is of the will, and faith which is of the understanding; because love was everything, and faith was of love. But after faith was separated from love, as was the case with those who were called
the will had no longer any rule; but as... faith reigned in that mind instead of love, it is said that he
dwelt towards the east of Eden;
for faith was distinguished, or had a mark set on it, that it might be preserved for the use of mankind.
Lamech, who was the sixth in order, altogether denied even faith.
It belongs to faith to understand not only what is true, but also what is good; the Knowledges of faith involve both; but to be such as faith teaches is celestial.
= faith, or the things which are of love and of faith thence in one complex.
(also) = the faith of that Church, which was the faith of charity. So the Lord foresaw, that the human race could be saved through the faith of charity.
As love is the containant of faith, and faith is the containant of the Knowledges of faith.
Faith is only the form of love... and the faith is thence formed according to the quality of the love or charity.
= to understand, and to have faith. (

, References.) To know Truths, to acknowledge Truths, and to have faith in Truths, are three completely different things. To know is the first of regeneration, to acknowledge is the second, and to have faith is the third... Infidels can acknowledge, and when in certain states, can from zeal preach, confirm, and persuade; but none can have faith except the faithful. They who have faith know, acknowledge, and believe; they have charity; they have conscience; and therefore faith can never be predicated, that is, it cannot be said of anyone that he has faith, unless he is of this character. Merely to know what is of faith, belongs to the memory without the consent of its Rational; to acknowledge what is of faith, is a certain Rational consenting, being induced to do so by certain causes, and for the sake of certain ends; but to have faith is of the conscience, that is, of the Lord operating through the conscience... In the other life, many who only know (and also many who only acknowledge) are in Hell... But they who have had faith are all in Heaven.
By faith... is meant charity from which is faith; for no other faith exists, which is faith, except the faith of charity.
When on account of the voluntary proprium of man, the faith of charity does not appear. Signified.
= the faith (which is derived from charity), and all things which are of faith...
= that he wanted to investigate the things that are of faith... by reasonings. Illustrated.
For faith is no other than of charity; and, essentially, is charity itself...
It is as impossible to acquire faith from these (reasonings) as...

As they are devoid of charity, they do not know what faith is. When asked, they can only reply that it is a kind of thought; some, that it is confidence; others, that it is the Knowledges of faith; a few, that it is a life according to Knowledges; and scarcely any that it is the life of charity or of mutual love.
Faith is the acknowledgement of those things which belong to faith; and the acknowledgement is never external but internal, and is the operation of the Lord alone through the charity with the man.

They do not know that love to the Lord and love towards the neighbour are faith itself; and that the Knowledges which they call faith have no end but (the reception of these loves); and that this is the faith which saves.
The first-born of every Church, in the internal sense, is faith.
= according to the differences as to faith.
A good Spirit is known not only as to the goodness, but also as to the faith in which he is.
That heavenly things would be given to those who have faith in the Lord. Signified.
There are two things in the internal man, love and faith; and these two constitute a one when faith is from love.
Faith and the things of faith are nothing but truths.

The conjunction of men with the Lord is effected through... the implantation of faith in love. Unless faith is implanted in love; that is, unless a man, through the things which are of faith, receives the life of faith, that is, charity, there is no conjunction.

By the faith which is the internal of the Church is meant no other than that which is of love and charity; that is, which is from love or charity. In a general sense, faith is everything doctrinal of the Church; but what is doctrinal separated from love or charity never makes the internal of the Church... That (the former) is the faith which is the internal of the Church, may be evident from this fact alone, that he who has the life of charity knows all things of faith.
When there is no faith, that is, no charity...
The Celestial Spiritual... is faith in which there is charity, or faith which is generated from charity.
They who learn Knowledges in order to be perfected in the faith of love

elements.injection1: for true and real faith is love to the Lord and towards the neighbour

elements.str: When faith or truth is treated of...
Conjunction with those who have faith in Him. Signified.
= the things which are generated and born from charity, that is, all things of faith; or, what is the same, all those who are regenerated by the Lord, thus in whom there is the faith of charity.

here, = those who have the faith of love, that is, love to the Lord, thus the celestial... Whereas they who have the faith of charity, that is, charity towards the neighbour, thus the spiritual... are signified by
The saying that those are saved who have faith is true, but by
nothing else is meant in the Word than love to the Lord and charity towards the neighbour, thus the life thence. The doctrinal things and dogmas of faith are not faith, but of faith...
Holiness is never predicated... of faith, except in the proportion that there are love and charity in the truths of faith.
In the good of charity with man are... all things of his faith.
The love of the world is diametrically opposite to the spiritual things of faith; and the love of self, to the celestial things of love.
The essential things of faith, being necessary to salvation, are expressed in the letter such as they are in the internal sense.

Many say that man is saved by faith; or, as they say, if only he has faith; but most of them do not know what faith is; some suppose that it is mere thought; some, that it is the acknowledgement of something that is to be believed; others, that it is the whole doctrine of faith which is to be believed... Thus they err in the mere Knowledge of what faith is.

It is this heavenly life which is regarded by all those things which are called faith; and it is procured by all things of faith. Hence it may be evident what faith is, namely, that it is charity; for to this lead all things which are called the doctrines of faith...
Faith from charity is like the light in the time of spring and summer, by which all things germinate and flourish; (for) love and charity is celestial flame, and faith is the spiritual light thence.
precedes, because love comes through faith; but when
precedes, it = that faith is from love.
I will betroth thee unto Me in faith
The desolation of faith, which is effected by falsities. Treated of.
They do not even know that the fundamental of faith is love to the Lord and charity towards the neighbour.
Hence, faith itself, in the internal sense, is nothing else than charity.

= to have faith... The reason it here = conscience, is that those who have faith have conscience too; the former is inseparable from the latter, and in fact so inseparable, that whether you say faith or conscience is all the same. By faith is meant the faith by which comes charity, and which is from charity, thus is charity itself; for faith without charity is no faith.
= the state of the Church before the last, when there begins to be no faith.
As the conjunction of the Lord with mankind is effected through love and charity, and the faith thence...

For the good of charity is the very ground of the seeds of faith... and therefore in proportion as a man is in... charity, he is in faith, especially in this principal of faith, that all salvation is from the Lord.
That no one can have faith unless he is in charity, is evident from
From these passages it is evident that love to the Lord, and charity towards the neighbour, is the life of faith. Explained.
Here is described the first state of the vastated Church, when there begins to be no faith, because no charity.

They may suppose that they can easily receive faith (after death), when they see that the Lord rules the universal Heaven... but it is as far from being possible for the evil to receive faith... as Hell is from Heaven...
That they are saved who are in the affection of truth, that is, who are in faith, provided it is the faith of good. Signified.
The spiritual things of faith are all the truths which are from good.
The good of doctrine is love and charity; the truth of doctrine is faith.
Those think from the affirmative who believe that they are truths because the Lord says so in the Word, thus who have faith in the Lord.
They who are in love to the Lord and charity towards the neighbour are able to... have faith in the Word; but not they who are in the love of self and of the world...
In (this gentile) there was the mercy which is of love, and in his ignorance there was innocence; and when these are present, all things of faith are received as it were spontaneously.
Persuasive light... induces a faith of falsity by truths, and a faith of truth by falsities.
= the understanding, the Spiritual of which is faith.
They apprehended with the understanding and had faith, which is to
The sight of the understanding is from the light of Heaven flowing into those things which are of the light of the world; but the sight of faith is from the light of Heaven.
It is this union (of the Divine and the Human) by which they can be saved who have the faith of charity in Him.
The confirmation of an idea by many things causes... that faith can be insinuated into it.
= the faith of charity, or... those who are in the faith of charity, that is, the spiritual.
No others are in the faith of charity than they who are within the Church; for the faith of charity is the truth of doctrine adjoined to the good of life.

The truth of doctrine, or faith, is insinuated by an external way, and is carried into the memory; and is called forth thence by the Lord in its own time and order, and is conjoined with the affection of good. This is effected in the freedom of man... Such is the insemination and inrooting of faith: whatever is effected in freedom is conjoined...
(Thus) the truth of doctrine or faith can only be received by the affection of it.
The reception of faith with those who are of the Church. Treated of.
When there is no longer any faith, that is (or because there is no) charity.
What is obscure of faith. Signified.
doctrinal things; because these introduce to faith.
They are here said to be
because they are in the progression of receiving faith; for from faith, namely, from its good, they receive life, of which this is the only source.

Quite different is the case with the Churches which say that faith is the essential of the Church... They say, indeed, that the veriest faith which saves is trust, but this trust is possible only in the good of life...
In the proper sense, Truth signifies the same as faith; in the Hebrew language, too, faith is expressed by such a word; so that that which is called
in the Old Testament is called

in the New Testament; and therefore it has been so often said that truth is of faith... But, in the internal sense, faith is nothing but charity; and there is no faith except by love. References... For all faith is from charity...
Unless truth is learned from affection, thus in freedom, it is not... exalted towards the interiors, and there made faith.

Such is the rooting of faith, or of the truth which is of faith, that unless it is coupled with good in the Rational, the truth of faith never receives any life, nor is any fruit produced thence; for that which is called the fruit of faith is the fruit of the good which is of love and charity through the truth which is of faith.
When the truth of faith is received by the will... faith is of charity, or as to life is charity itself.
Unless the truth of faith... is received by the good of love... it is not faith.
Causes... the truth (in the natural man) to receive the rays of light, that is, faith.
= those who are in charity through faith, that is, the spiritual.

In order that the spiritual man may have the truth of faith, or faith, it must come from the new understanding with which he is endowed by the Lord, and the new understanding must have its light from the new will.
They who are of the Spiritual Church are in faith, namely, in its good and truth... The truth which the spiritual have is that of faith, so far as this is doctrine concerning charity.

No one is admitted into the Lord's Kingdom unless he is in the good of faith... Still, they who are in the truth of faith, that is, who profess faith, and call it the essential thing... and yet are in the good of life... are in the Lord's Spiritual Kingdom.
The Lord's Spiritual Kingdom in the Heavens is... various as to the things which are of faith.
The struggle as to whether... charity which is of good or faith which is of truth is the prior. Treated of.
To look from faith, and not from love and charity, is to look behind, and to return back.
= those who are in the faith of charity.
The Church then recedes successively from charity, and turns aside to faith... Signified.
These ideas surpass not only apprehension, but also faith.
The state of the Lord as to the things which are of faith relatively to the rational things which were to be adjoined. Signified.

If truths Divine themselves were opened, they would not be received by those who are in the doctrinal things of faith, because they surpass all their rational apprehension, thus all their faith. Signified.
The man who... cannot do otherwise than profane, is withheld as far as possible from the acknowledgement and faith of truth and good.

They who are in the mere doctrinal things of faith, and not in the good of life, cannot but be in persuasive faith... But in proportion as anyone is in persuasive faith, he is stupid; but in proportion as anyone is in the good of life... he is in intelligence, that is, in faith from the Lord.

Conjunction is effected with those who... although they make faith the essential thing as to doctrine, still make charity the essential thing as to life; for with these there is confidence or trust in the Lord, which they call faith itself... Treated of.
Love and charity is spiritual conjunction, but not faith, except through love and charity.
That faith in the Lord would expire, according to the degrees in which charity would cease. Signified.
= conjunction with Him through the faith of love.
States of faith are according to states of charity. Example(s).
When the order begins from love, everything which follows thence in genuine order appears flaming; but when the order begins from faith, everything... appears lucid...

signifies is faith. The reason faith is the first universal, is from the fact that when man is being regenerated... he must first learn and imbue the things which are of faith, that is, which are of spiritual truth...

Regarded in itself, faith is faith in the understanding and faith in the will; to know and to understand the truth which is of faith is called faith in the understanding; whereas to will the truth which is of faith is called faith in the will. Faith in the understanding is that which is signified by
and faith in the will is that which is signified by
That faith in the understanding, or the understanding of truth, precedes faith in the will, or the willing of truth, may be evident to everyone...
in the internal sense, = faith from the Lord, is evident from the fact, that the interior understanding has no other objects than the things which are of truth and good, for these are of faith.
= to believe in Him, thus to see Him by faith; for they who are in faith, from faith see God; for God is in faith; and God is that in the faith which is truly faith.
= to have faith; for the Lord is seen only by faith; for faith is the eye of love; for by love through faith the Lord is seen; and love is the life of faith; and therefore it is said
Ye shall see Me; because I live, ye shall live also.

= faith from the Lord; for no other faith exists, which is faith, except that which is from the Lord; this, also, gives man to see, that is, to believe. But faith from self, or from the proprium of man, is not faith; for this causes him to see falsities as truths, and truths as falsities; and even if he sees truths as truths, still he does not see them, because he does not believe them; for he sees himself in them, and not the Lord.

The light of Heaven, being from the Lord, has with it intelligence and wisdom, consequently faith in Him; for faith in the Lord is within intelligence and wisdom; and therefore to see from that light... can signify nothing but faith in the Lord... It is this light which shines in the consciences of those who have faith in Him...

By faith, when it is distinguished from charity, is meant truth, such as is that of doctrine, or such as is contained in the confession which is called the Apostolic Faith; and this according to the general meaning of the word in the Church; for to have faith in truths is believed to be the faith by which there is salvation.
The state of faith if the will does not correspond to it. Signified.
The cardiac motions with them are according to the states of love; and the respiratory ones are according to the states of faith.
The truths of faith which are not learned for the sake of acting... are not of faith with him who learned them, but interiorly are against faith.
= all things of faith and love.

in the internal sense, is the holy of faith, is that faith which is predicated of truth corresponds to the Divine justice... And the reason, why, in the external sense, it = the good of life, is (that) the holy of faith corresponds to the good of life.
They who reason about truth from... the negative, destroy all things of faith. Signified.
That they were in the negative as to all things of faith. Signified.
The works of faith, which from the appearance may also be called its fruits.
Faith as to its state of love and charity. Signified.
They have not the truth of faith who believe that they have faith from self, thus are wise from self; but they have it who believe from the Lord; for to them faith and wisdom is given...
They had depended upon the faith of others...
Therefore man is in Heaven as to his interiors, when he is in spiritual love and faith.
Consequently, he acknowledges all things which confirm love and charity, which are called the things of faith...
The evil which a man has confirmed... even to faith and persuasion, cannot be amended.
= a state of faith or truth; and
a state of no faith or truth.
The gentiles who have lived in mutual charity... in the other life receive faith more easily... than those within the Church who have not lived in such charity.
The inward quality of those who have only a scientific faith, shown.
He can confirm this by a number of his own experiences, if he is once in the faith that it is so.
The rock on which the Church will be built
With the spiritual man, this light falls into the things which are of faith with him... but with the celestial man, into the good of love.
Hence it was evident why they who lead a life of evil, can never, from a sincere heart, have faith in Divine truths...
= from the faith of all falsities.

For he who is in the works of charity, or, what is the same, in the life of faith, is in the capacity of receiving faith, if not in the body, still in the other life; but he who is not in the works of charity... is in no capacity whatever of receiving faith, neither in the body, nor in the other life...
Every Church which commences from faith is such (as to quickly turn aside)... It has no other director than the understanding; and the understanding no other than that which is hereditary to man...
For faith is from Him through good.
= the things which are of faith; (for) they represent the Church which turns aside from charity to faith; and afterwards to faith separated from charity.
Those who were in faith, namely, in the faith of some charity. Signified.

The (ancients) did not know anything about faith, as the Christian Church does, but about Truth. Truth to them was the same as faith is to Christians; and in the Original Language there is the same word for both.

But the Christian Church gives the name of faith to those doctrinal things which are the interiors of the Church, and are said to be what must be believed; for by faith the common people mean no other than the faith of creeds...
Those are said to fall from the general truth of the Church who acknowledge faith as essential, but not charity.
It treats of the Church which commences from faith, which from the very beginning it thus separates from charity...
But if the Church would acknowledge the life of faith as a principle, it would acknowledge charity towards the neighbour and love to the Lord, and hence the works of charity and love...
The Church which commences from faith would cease to be a Church, unless this Divine truth remained in it, that the Human of the Lord is Divine. Signified.
When (those who are in the affirmative) consult scientifics, they... corroborate faith...
That there was no longer any faith. Signified.
It cast Truth to the earth
= that it cast down faith itself which in itself is charity; for faith regards charity, because it proceeds from charity.
Unless man is in the affection of good, and thence in faith in the Lord.
The sons by Tamar = the two essentials of the Church, namely, faith and love;
love. Their birth represents that love is actually the first-born of the Church, and that faith is only apparently so.
Unless there were light from good within man, he could never see truths to acknowledgement and faith.
To receive Divine truth is not only to have faith but also to act faith...

The case with faith is this. He that receives it, and that has it, is continually in the remembrance of the Lord, even when he is thinking or speaking about something else... for the remembrance of the Lord, on the part of those who are in faith, reigns universally...
The sphere of faith from charity is the sphere which reigns in Heaven...

The reception of faith is treated of, because the Sensuous, like the Rational, is re-born by faith, but by that faith into which charity flows; for unless charity flows into faith, and gives it life, faith cannot universally reign; since that reigns which a man loves...
When the faith of charity is the end... if there is correspondence, then faith from charity flows into the thought...
When faith is received in the exterior Natural... correspondence is effected, and charity is received... Treated of.
Hence from the life it may be known what is the quality of the faith; for good and evil are of the life, and truth and falsity are of the faith.
Therefore when there is no subordination (of the exterior Natural), a man cannot have any... faith.
Conjunction is effected by means of faith.
= the things which are of faith... Spiritual look is faith.
This image, being interior, appears only to those who are in faith from charity.
= the things which are not of faith.
Acknowledgement through faith, and adoration. Signified.

They who are in the affection of truth for the sake of truth and of life... have indeed faith in the doctrinal things of the Church; but still they search the Word... and thence have their faith and their conscience.
That all things of faith are thus conjoined together. Signified.
That faith in the will will be separated. Signified, Explained.
When there is faith in the will, truths become goods. Signified, Explained.
To trust to scientifics in the things of faith, and not to have faith in any spiritual truth, unless what is scientific and sensuous dictates it. Signified.

(Thus) what is scientific is by no means to be rejected from the truths of faith, but they are to be conjoined; by the prior way, however, that is, by the way from faith; and not by the posterior way, that is, by the way from scientifics.
Such have faith in those whom they believe to be enlightened.
How it is to be understood that through faith there is power in good, and the first power in truth. Explained, Signified.
At the beginning of regeneration, faith is in obscurity. Signified.
The Lord continually flows in through the internal of man with good and truth; the good gives life and its heat, which is love; and the truth gives enlightenment and its light, which is faith.
With those who are in... persuasive faith, the ideas of thought are exceedingly confined.
Chiding, because one wanted to destroy the faith of another. Signified.

Dost thou want to destroy my faith? Signified. Faith is of the Church; and these two things are so united, that he who destroys faith with anyone, destroys the Church with him; and this is to kill him; for he who takes away faith, takes away spiritual life.
That He endowed the Church with faith. Signified.
That if the Spiritual Church had not hope and faith they would be dragged down by falsities, evils, and profane things. Treated of.
Hence it is that no faith can ever be implanted in those of the Spiritual Church, unless with a mighty force they are withheld by the Lord from falsities. Signified, Explained.
That they may have faith concerning the Lord's Divine Human. Signified.

They who are of the Spiritual Church, in childhood, and afterwards in adolescence, have faith in the doctrinal things of their own Church; but at that time they have faith from their parents and masters, and not from themselves; and therefore if they afterwards recede from faith, they profane truth only slightly... Whereas if a man has faith in the doctrine of the Church and in the Word from himself, that is, by means of confirmations with himself, if he afterwards recedes... he profanes truth...
Providence, what would be the quality of those of the Spiritual Church if they had faith. Signified.

To have faith, here, does not mean faith from the signs... for this faith is concerned with worldly things; but faith, that if they do not remain in truths, they will become merely sensuous and corporeal, and at last profaners of truth... Faith in worldly things is quite different from faith in spiritual things. Example(s).
Light in the natural world corresponds to faith in the Spiritual World... and faith is actually the light of man.
That they did not receive from faith and obedience. Signified.

The Spiritual Church with man begins through faith in knowledge and afterwards in understanding, which is represented by Reuben and his sons. Afterwards, when the Church grows with man, that faith passes into the will, and from the will into act; and then the man wills the truth of faith, and does it, because it is so commanded in the Word. This [state] of faith is represented by Simeon. At last the affection of charity is perceived in his will, which is new, so that he wills to do good, not as before, from faith, but from charity towards the neighbour... This... is represented by Levi.
As the case is so with the Spiritual Church, it is not wonderful that with most, faith is the essential of the Church, and not charity.
That miracles contribute nothing to faith. Illustrated.

represents those who have professed faith, and have also persuaded themselves that faith saves, and yet have lived contrary to the precepts of faith; in a word, who have been in persuasive faith, and in a life of evil. Explained. (Their state in the other life.)
By these are meant those who have been in miraculous faith, and not in the faith of the Church.
In proportion as a man is in the loves of self and of the world... he does not know what faith is, until at last he does not know that it is anything.
In order that this Scientific may become of faith, it must be conjoined with good, and it then passes into the internal man, and becomes faith.
That which enters by an external way is perceived... Hence it is, that everything of the Church is attributed to faith.
It is the affections of truth and of good which constitute faith.
Everyone's faith is such as is his life. If, therefore, the life is damned, so is the faith; for when the life is evil it is the faith of falsity.
This persuasive is also supposed to be faith, but it is not faith; for it is impressed from the end that it may serve as a means for securing gain, honours, and reputation. Signified.
Who does not know... that it is the life of faith which makes man spiritual...

Every spiritual good proceeds either from faith, that is, through faith, or from love... He who is in the first state cannot enter into the second until he is regenerated; and he who is in the second state ought not to betake himself to the first... He relapses into the state of faith which had served to introduce him to good, and also beyond it. Signified.
The sacrifices = the worship of the Lord from faith; and the burnt-offerings... from love.
Faith is an internal affection, which consists in this, that a man wills from the heart to know what is true and what is good, not for the sake of doctrine, but for the sake of life.
When faith is mentioned, there is meant all the truth which is for the Spiritual Church... and therefore the Spiritual Church itself is meant...
When man is being regenerated, he is led by faith in the understanding or by doctrine, to faith in the will or life...
That which is (as it were) conceived in the womb, and born from the womb, is not man as man, but is the faith of charity; for this constitutes the Spiritual of man...
That faith merely natural is not to be ascribed to the Lord; but the truth of innocence which is therein. Signified, Explained.
= that which is first born from a regenerate man, thus faith.

Faith merely natural is faith which is insinuated by an external way, and not by an internal one; as sensuous faith, which exists when a man believes that it is so, because the eye has seen it and the hand has touched it. (Signified by the Lord's words to Thomas). Also the faith of miracles, which exists when a man believes that it is so merely from miracles; and also the faith of authority, which exists when a man believes that it is so, because some one else, in whom he has faith, has said so. But spiritual faith is that which is insinuated by an internal and at the same time by an external way; insinuation by an internal way causes it to be believed, and then that which is insinuated by an external way causes it to be confirmed. The Spiritual of faith is the affection of charity, and thence the affection of truth for the sake of good use and for the sake of life; these cause faith to be spiritual. The insinuation of faith by an internal way is effected by the reading of the Word, and at the same time by enlightenment from the Lord, which is given according to the quality of the affection, that is, according to the end in the knowing of truth.
That the truths of faith are not to be ascribed to the Lord, but its goods. Signified.
For the Lord gives faith mediately by its good.
That therefore the faith of charity which is of the new generation, is to be ascribed to the Lord. Signified.

etc. are chiefly the falsities of those who are in persuasive faith, that is, who persuade themselves that the doctrinal things of the Church in which they are, are true, and yet are in a life of evil. Persuasive faith exists together with evil of life, but not saving faith; for persuasive faith is a persuasion that all things which are of the doctrine of the Church are truths... for the sake of profits... and reputation.

Saving faith is given by the Lord; but (persuasive faith) is from the man himself; the former remains to eternity, the latter is dissipated in the other life: it is also dissipated in the world, if they gain nothing by it; but so long as they gain by it they light for it as if for Heaven itself... They who are in this faith in the world, can with difficulty be distinguished from those who are in saving faith; for they speak and preach in favour of what is doctrinal with an ardour as of zeal, but it is an ardour from the fire of the love of self and of the world... In the other life they are vastated as to this faith.
An endeavour to subjugate those who are in faith conjoined with charity. Signified.
Trust is of love through faith; consequently, trust in... the Lord exists only with those who are in love to the Lord and towards the neighbour, because no others have faith.

That everything of faith and of the glory thence is from the Divine truth which is from Him. Signified. For all the glory which man has is from faith in the Lord; and thus the Lord is in faith, and therefore so is glory itself. (For) the Divine truth, from which and through which is faith, appears... as light.
In the other life everyone retains the principles of his faith which he had in the life of the body...

The interior (Angels of the Spiritual Kingdom) are those who are in charity itself, and thence in faith; but the exterior ones are those who are in faith, but not yet in charity: the latter do good from obedience; the former from affection.
The faith of the Lord's precepts. Signified.
He who leads a life of faith performs repentance daily...
No faith, and consequently no obedience. Signified.
= faith, here, faith from the Lord, or the Lord as to faith. Illustrated.

The reason (the power of opening and shutting Heaven and Hell) belongs to faith, is that faith is from the Lord, thus also is of the Lord, that is, the Lord Himself is in it: all power in the other life is through the truth of faith from good.
The faith which is from the Lord is from the Divine law, that is, from the Word; for by means of this the Lord teaches what faith is, and also gives faith.
Faith is given through truths, and, in fact, through the primary ones; for enlightenment is effected from these...
When Moses lifted up his hand
= when faith with those of the Spiritual Church looked to the Lord.
When he let down his hand
= when faith with them looked downwards, or from the Lord to self and the world.
The reason the faith which looks to the Lord conquers, is that the Lord then lights; for the Lord is faith, because faith is from Him...
They who are of the Spiritual Church cannot be in faith which continually looks to the Lord; but are alternately in faith which looks to self and the world. Signified.
They who have used knowledges as a means to annihilate the things which are of faith, have utterly destroyed their Intellectual...
He who does not know that the Lord is the Saviour of the world, cannot have faith in Him...
(Thus) the life of the regenerate man is the life of faith.
Action from the light of intelligence, thus from for faith from the Lord is in the light of intelligence. Signified.
Hence there is a correspondence... of light in the world with faith, which is thence called spiritual light.
They who believe... that the essential of worship is the life of faith, that is, charity towards the neighbour and love to the Lord, belong to the internal Church.
They belong to the external Church who do good to the neighbour and worship the Lord solely from the obedience of faith...
Love to God and love towards the neighbour... can exist only by means of faith.
That there may be a permanent faith of truth. Signified.
A veiling over of the interiors so that they may appear in the holy of faith... Signified.
For there to be a Church there must be with the man of the Church faith in the Lord, and also love to Him and love towards the neighbour.
The obscurity of faith, such as that of those of the Spiritual Church... Signified.
